claims.claim: IBM reported second-quarter 2026 revenue of $17.2 billion.
Second-quarter revenue was flat year over year on a GAAP basis.
claims.note: The release's income statement summary shows total revenue year/year of 1 (up 1 percent), not flat; revenue rose from $16,977M to $17,162M.

claims.claim: GAAP pre-tax income margin declined about one percentage point year over year to 14.4 percent.
Operating (non-GAAP) pre-tax income for the quarter was $3.3 billion.
Operating (non-GAAP) pre-tax income margin increased three percentage points versus the prior-year period.
claims.note: The release shows operating pre-tax income margin of 19.2 percent, up 0.3 points year over year (18.8 percent prior year). The 3 is the percent growth in operating pre-tax income dollars, not a margin point change.

claims.claim: Free cash flow for the quarter was $2.5 billion, down $0.3 billion year over year.
Net cash from operating activities for the quarter was $2.6 billion, up $0.9 billion year over year.
The company returned $1.6 billion to shareholders in dividends during the second quarter.
IBM ended the quarter with $8.2 billion in cash, restricted cash and marketable securities.
Software revenues totaled $7.8 billion, up five percent year over year.
Hybrid Cloud (Red Hat) grew eleven percent.
Data revenue rose nineteen percent.
Software growth was driven by strong performance in Hybrid Cloud (Red Hat) and Data.
Consulting revenues were $5.3 billion, flat year over year and up one percent at constant currency.
Strategy and Technology increased one percent at constant currency.
Intelligent Operations increased one percent at constant currency.
Infrastructure revenues declined seven percent to $3.8 billion.
IBM Z revenue fell forty-two percent.
The Infrastructure decline was primarily due to the drop in IBM Z.
Distributed Infrastructure grew thirty-seven percent.
Power and Storage built up an order backlog of nearly $500 million.
Financing revenues increased twelve percent to $0.2 billion, up eleven percent at constant currency.
Management now expects full-year 2026 constant currency revenue growth in the range of four-to-five percent.
At current foreign exchange rates, currency is expected to be neutral to growth for the year.
The company continues to expect full-year free cash flow to increase by about $1 billion year over year.
The company anticipates improved pre-tax income margin expansion for the full year.
No specific guidance was provided regarding third-quarter results or adjusted earnings per share.
IBM invested $10.5 billion in acquisitions during the first six months of 2026.
Debt, including IBM Financing debt of $13.0 billion, totaled $62.0 billion as of June 30, 2026.
Capital expenditures for the quarter were $229 million.
claims.note: The release's free cash flow reconciliation shows capital expenditures, net of $359 million for the quarter. The $229 million figure is only 'Payments for property, plant and equipment' and excludes the $154 million investment in software; treating it as capital expenditures misstates the basis.

claims.claim: The company purchased marketable securities totaling $1.259 billion in the quarter.
The company received $1.152 billion from disposition of investments in the quarter.
Total assets were $152.1 billion.
Goodwill was $74.6 billion.
Intangibles, net were $14.0 billion.
GAAP revenue performance was flat (Watch items).
claims.note: Repeats the error from the Results section; the release reports total revenue up 1 percent year over year.

claims.claim: AI adoption is moving from experimentation to enterprise-scale deployment.
IBM Z revenues declined forty-two percent (Watch items).
Cash and marketable securities were reduced by $6.3 billion year over year.
claims.note: The release states cash, restricted cash and marketable securities of $8.2 billion was down $6.3 billion from year-end 2025 (a six-month change), not a year-over-year change.
